overview.description: Ansible playbooks in IBM Technology Zone provide post-deploy customization and pre-destroy cleanup for environment definitions. This guide covers creating playbooks for all supported platforms following official standards.

type.name: post-deploy
type.purpose: Configure and customize environments after initial provisioning

type.name: pre-destroy
type.purpose: Cleanup and backup before environment destruction

playbook_structure.description: Playbooks for IBM Cloud Services run on provisioning infrastructure with access to IBM Cloud API and CLI. They parse deployment variables and configure IBM Cloud services.
playbook_structure.standard_template:
--- - name: IBMCloud Account Vending hosts: localhost gather_facts: false
vars: delay_seconds: 10 retry_count: 3 cloud_region: "us-south"
tasks: ############################################ # Gather all variables ############################################ - name: Parse deployment variables tags: [parse, setup] block: - name: Set backward compatibility variables set_fact: account_vars: "{{ account_variables | default(itz.deployment.account_variables | default('{}')) }}" environment_vars: "{{ environment_variables | default(itz.deployment.environment_variables | default('{}')) }}" group_vars: "{{ group_variables | default(itz.deployment.group_variables | default('{}')) }}" idp_vars: "{{ idp_variables | default(itz.deployment.idp_variables | default('{}')) }}" service_instance_vars: "{{ service_instance_variables | default(itz.deployment.service_instance_variables | default('{}')) }}" extra_vars: "{{ extra_variables | default(itz.deployment.extra_variables | default('{}')) }}"
# Parse each variable type with string/dict detection [Include variable parsing for all six types]
rescue: - name: Handle parsing failures debug: msg: "Critical error during variable parsing."
- name: Fail playbook on critical parsing errors fail: msg: "Unable to continue due to critical parsing errors."
# Set facts from parsed JSON - name: Set facts from supplied json data ansible.builtin.set_fact: account_apikey: "{{ account_json['account_api_key'] }}" account_name: "{{ account_json['account_name'] }}" account_id: "{{ account_json['account_id'] }}"
############################################ # IBM Cloud Authentication ############################################ - name: Connect to IBM Cloud account ansible.builtin.uri: url: "https://iam.cloud.ibm.com/identity/token" method: POST return_content: yes body_format: form-urlencoded body: apikey: "{{ account_apikey }}" grant_type: "urn:ibm:params:oauth:grant-type:apikey" register: token_response delay: "{{ delay_seconds }}" retries: "{{ retry_count }}"
- name: Set fact access_token ansible.builtin.set_fact: access_token: "{{ token_response['json'].access_token }}"
############################################ # Service Configuration Tasks ############################################ [Add service-specific tasks here]
############################################ # Post-Deploy Output ############################################ - name: Create post-deploy HTML output file ansible.builtin.copy: dest: ../post_deploy_text_output.txt content: | [HTML formatted output] mode: '0644'

variable_parsing_requirements.requirement: Parse all six variable types (account, environment, group, idp, service_instance, extra)
Detect if variable is string or dictionary
Use from_json filter for string variables
Use direct access for dictionary variables
Include error handling with rescue blocks

authentication_requirements.requirement: Obtain bearer token from IBM Cloud IAM
Use token in Authorization headers for API calls
Set up IBM Cloud CLI authentication for command execution
Use no_log: true for sensitive data

playbook_structure.description: Playbooks for Base VMs run during Cloud-Init phase on RedHat 9.x systems. They have direct access to the VM and use infrastructure variables.
playbook_structure.standard_template:
--- ################################################################################ # Playbook: post-[name].yml # Purpose: [Brief description of what this playbook does] # Usage: ansible-playbook post-[name].yml -e "variable='value'" ################################################################################
- name: [Descriptive Task Name] hosts: 127.0.0.1 become: true gather_facts: true
vars: # Variables are passed from environment override post_deploy_variables [variable_name]: [default_value] # Use hard-coded defaults, NOT | default() filters
tasks: # ------------------------------------------------------------------ # Input Variable Processing # ------------------------------------------------------------------
- name: Display loaded variables that are needed ansible.builtin.debug: msg: | Variables from reservation: [variable_name]: {{ [variable_name] }}
############################################ # System Updates and Package Installation ############################################
- name: Update system packages ansible.builtin.dnf: name: "*" state: latest update_cache: true register: dnf_update retries: 3 delay: 5 until: dnf_update is succeeded
############################################ # Service Configuration ############################################
[Add service-specific configuration tasks]
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ # Post-Deploy Output Generation # ------------------------------------------------------------------ - name: Create post-deploy HTML output file ansible.builtin.copy: dest: ../post_deploy_text_output.txt content: | [HTML formatted output] mode: '0644'
handlers: [Optional handlers for service restarts]

rule.name: No Default Filters
rule.rationale: Variables are passed from environment override. Hard-coded defaults ensure predictable behavior.

rule.name: Execution Context
rule.rationale: Playbooks run during Cloud-Init on the VM itself

rule.name: Package Management
rule.requirement: Include retry logic for network operations

playbook_structure.description: Playbooks for OpenShift clusters use GitOps-based deployment with ArgoCD integration. They configure cluster resources and applications.

characteristics.characteristic: Access to OpenShift API and CLI

pattern.name: service_name_resolution
pattern.description: Convert marketing names to programmatic names using IBM Cloud Global Catalog

process.step: Query IBM Cloud Global Catalog API: https://globalcatalog.cloud.ibm.com/api/v1

pattern.name: retry_logic
pattern.description: Network-dependent operations should include retry logic
pattern.template: - name: Operation with retry ansible.builtin.[module]: [parameters] register: result retries: 3 delay: 5 until: result is succeeded

pattern.name: post_deploy_output
pattern.description: Generate HTML-formatted output for IBM Technology Zone UI

requirements.requirement: Include: Account/VM details, service status, next steps
Use: IBM Technology Zone standard styling

css_classes.class: Table cells with light blue background

pattern.name: error_handling
pattern.description: Proper error handling with rescue blocks
pattern.template:
- name: Critical operation block: [tasks] rescue: - name: Log error debug: msg: "Error occurred: {{ ansible_failed_result.msg }}"
- name: Fail with context fail: msg: "Failed to complete operation: [context]"

pattern.name: service_verification
pattern.template:
- name: Start service ansible.builtin.systemd: name: [service-name] state: started register: service_status
- name: Verify service is running ansible.builtin.systemd: name: [service-name] register: service_check failed_when: service_check.status.ActiveState != "active"

requirement.name: Generate Complete Playbook
requirement.description: Output ONLY the Ansible playbook YAML, no additional text

requirement.name: Include Header Comment
requirement.description: Use standardized comment block with playbook name, purpose, and usage

requirement.name: Follow Platform Structure
requirement.description: Use the correct structure for the target platform

requirement.name: Verify Service Status
requirement.description: Include verification tasks after service configuration

environment_definition_integration.description: After generating the playbook, provide the environment definition variables showing how to reference and configure the playbook.
environment_definition_integration.example_for_vm_platforms:
# Environment Definition Variables post_deploy_variables: - key: custom_variable value: "example_value" type: string description: "Description of the variable"
# Reference the playbook post_deploy_script: | ansible-playbook post-[name].yml \ -e "custom_variable={{ custom_variable }}"
environment_definition_integration.example_for_cloud_services:
# Environment Definition Variables post_deploy_playbook: "post-[name].yml"
# Variables are automatically passed as JSON # No additional configuration needed

validation_checklist.check: Header comment block is complete and accurate
Variables use hard-coded defaults (no | default() filters) for VM platforms
Service names are programmatic (verified via IBM Cloud Global Catalog)
Service status is verified after starting
Handlers are defined for service restarts (if needed)
No sensitive data in debug output (use no_log: true)

security_guidelines.guideline: Use no_log: true for tasks handling sensitive data (API keys, passwords)
Never display API keys or tokens in debug output
Follow principle of least privilege for service accounts
Do not install unauthorized or malicious software
Do not create higher tier service plans without authorization
